sources.citation: Osaji, Bede. 1979. Language Survey in Nigeria. Publication B-81. Quebec: International Center for Research on Bilingualism, Laval University (ERIC microfiche).
sources.note: Entry 'Dungi: Kaduna State, Saminaka Division, Lere District; 310 (NAT 1949); Benue-Congo: Western Plateau.' Location, population and classification only.

sources.citation: HRAF file FF38 Katab (processed 1960), containing excerpts of Gunn, Harold D. 1956. Pagan peoples of the central area of northern Nigeria (Katab section), Meek 1931, Temple 1922 and Cole (archive.org microfiche scanned).
sources.note: 'Dungi' occurs only in a map legend ('Tribes of Lere and Kauru Districts.. Dungi 10') and a 1949 tribal-statistics table; no remark on the language. Gunn's own Lere/Kauru chapter is not in this HRAF file.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1, languoid dung1254 (Hammarström et al.), read online.
sources.note: Language marked 'Unattested'; only Campbell et al. 2022 endangerment citation; Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-67. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210 (Hamburg University Press, open access).
sources.note: Nothing about Dungu at all beyond Table 1 (pp. 48-49), where Dungu's Status and Source cells are '?' and p. 48 says '? signifies no information.' The 3.1 'Tones' section (pp. 57-58) describes Boze (four level tones) and tiMap only; stress is never mentioned for any East Kainji language.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press (CC-BY).
sources.note: Dungu is only a leaf in the East Kainji tree (Figure 7, p. 83). p. 82: 'Data for many languages consists of fragmentary wordlists, often orthographic with no tones or plurals.' No Dungu data, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. [2011/2019 draft]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd edition. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 94 'Dungu', p. 20.
sources.note: Entry gives names, location (Kaduna State, Saminaka LGA), population 310 (NAT 1949) and classification (Kainji: Eastern Kainji: Northern Jos: Kauru); it has NO Source(s) or Refs line, i.e. Blench knows no data source for Dungu. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004. The status of the East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: recent research. Ms., Cambridge, 12 pp. (version for the Hamburg meeting, March 2004).
sources.note: Dungu appears only as a name in Appendix 1 (Kauru list, p. 10) and in the 'arm, hand' table of Appendix 3 (p. 12) with an empty data row. The Tones section (p. 5) concerns eBoze/tiMap only; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Sommer, Gabriele. 1992. A survey on language death in Africa. In M. Brenzinger (ed.), Language Death: Factual and Theoretical Explorations, 301-413. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.note: Glottolog-listed overview for dung1254; may name the colonial-era source behind the 'Dungi' endangerment entry.

sources.citation: Temple, Olive (comp.), C. L. Temple (ed.). 1922. Notes on the tribes, provinces, emirates and states of the Northern Provinces of Nigeria. Lagos: CMS Bookshop.
sources.note: Glottolog cites it for the neighbouring Kauru languages (Kaivi, Kinuku, Tumi, Vono, Ruma, Bina); a 'Dungawa/Dungi' paragraph would be ethnographic only, but it is the earliest possible mention.
